response.sql: WITH actor_counts AS (SELECT f.film_id, COUNT(fa.actor_id) as actor_count FROM film f LEFT JOIN film_actor fa ON f.film_id = fa.film_id GROUP BY f.film_id), first_avg AS (SELECT AVG(actor_count) as avg1 FROM actor_counts), above_first AS (SELECT ac.film_id, ac.actor_count, fa.avg1 FROM actor_counts ac CROSS JOIN first_avg fa WHERE ac.actor_count > fa.avg1 AND fa.avg1 IS NOT NULL), second_avg AS (SELECT AVG(actor_count) as avg2 FROM above_first), above_second AS (SELECT af.film_id, af.actor_count, af.avg1, sa.avg2 FROM above_first af CROSS JOIN second_avg sa WHERE af.actor_count > sa.avg2 AND sa.avg2 IS NOT NULL) SELECT SUM(actor_count) as total_actors, AVG(actor_count - avg1) as avg_excess_over_first, AVG(actor_count - avg2) as avg_excess_over_second FROM above_second WHERE avg1 IS NOT NULL AND avg2 IS NOT NULL

assumptions.assumption: Films are included in the first average even if they have 0 actors (i.e., films that do not appear in film_actor). The phrase 'ignoring missing values' is interpreted as excluding NULL counts—which COUNT never produces—not as excluding films without actors.

alternatives.interpretation: If 'ignoring missing values' means excluding films with 0 actors entirely, count only films that have at least one actor in the film_actor table.
